# RFC 0048: An entry is generated by its structure and kept by its coverage

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2026-09-04
- Affects: `ring/tests/entries.rs`, `ring/entries-corpus.txt`,
  `claims/0009-entry-validation-coverage.toml`, `ring/Cargo.toml`,
  `ring/src/lib.rs`, `ring/src/registry.rs`, `xtask/src/main.rs`,
  `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `docs/test-taxonomy.md` and `.toml`,
  `docs/design/proving-ground.html` layer 4

## Decision

`E1-P05`'s fuzzer generates a submission entry from a list of named *families* —
a real opcode with a flag this build does not know, a live set id with an index
one past the set, a length one byte past the arena, a registration whose region
does not divide — and spends **one eighth** of its budget on byte-level
mutation. It runs under a per-case coverage signal read out of the LLVM profile
runtime's own counters, keeps the inputs that reach a region nothing had reached,
minimises them into `ring/entries-corpus.txt`, and publishes **the share of a
named list of thirty-seven functions that corpus covers** as a gating claim.

Five things that follow, each of which somebody could reasonably have decided the
other way:

1. **The path is a list of functions, written down twice on purpose.**
   `claims/0009`'s `path` and `ENTRIES_PATH` in `xtask` hold the same
   thirty-seven names and a check requires them to be the same set on every run.
   *95% of the validation path* means nothing until somebody says which lines are
   in it, so the list is the claim and the number is a consequence.
2. **The number is measured from the committed corpus and not from a drawn run.**
   A figure over a seeded run says the generator reaches the path. A figure over
   the file says a stranger with this checkout reaches it, in seconds, with no
   seed — which is what makes the corpus a release content rather than a
   souvenir.
3. **Three oracles, not one property.** *No panic* is
   `ring/tests/hostile.rs`'s and it is already checked nine orders of magnitude
   harder. What this file asks is whether the answer was *right*: the envelope
   refused with the code R04 names, an id never reissued, a resolved buffer
   inside its own set.
4. **The corpus carries hand-written seeds beside the coverage-fed cover**,
   because the signal is blind to part of the path and a measurement found out.
5. **A case is self-contained**, so a corpus line is a whole input — a named
   world and an entry — rather than a seed and an episode index.

## Context

`E1-P04` landed one task earlier and this is its sibling. That file draws a
hostile *peer* — header, cursors, index ring, epoch — and asks whether the honest
end panics, hangs or reads out of bounds. It draws a billion times and it cannot
tell a service that answered correctly from one that answered wrongly, because
nothing in it knows what the answer should be. `execute` masking an unknown flag
bit off instead of refusing it is invisible to every property that file asserts:
nothing panics, nothing hangs, nothing reads out of bounds, and two peers now
disagree about what happened. That defect is `mutate-ignored-flag`, it is one
character of difference, and it is exactly the class R04 exists to name.

So the two files share their corpus format, their episode discipline, their
argument parser's shape and their `harness = false` arrangement — because two
fuzzers with two of each is how one of them stops being maintained — and differ
in the only place that matters, which is the oracle.

### What the proportion is for

An `Sqe` is a typed record whose first check is *the reserved word is zero*.
Sixty-four uniformly random bytes carry a non-zero reserved word with probability
`1 - 2^-32`, so a byte-flipping fuzzer spends essentially its whole budget on the
first branch of the first check. This is measured rather than predicted:
`ring/tests/hostile.rs`'s `refused_flag` and `refused_opcode` counters sat at zero
through a clean billion draws for exactly that reason, and the fix there was two
extra cases in one function.

Hence fifty-six weights in sixty-four for structure and eight for bytes. The
eight are not zero because a list of families is a guess about where bugs live,
and a guess is not a proof. The run counts every family and `claims/0009` puts a
minimum on each, because a proportion in a comment is a proportion nobody checks.

### What per-input coverage actually costs

`cargo xtask coverage` has existed since M0 and reports a per-crate figure at
process exit. That is not feedback: feedback needs coverage *per input*, and a
profile written at exit is one number for a whole run.

The profile runtime exports three symbols — `__llvm_profile_begin_counters`,
`__llvm_profile_end_counters`, `__llvm_profile_reset_counters` — and with them
the harness resets the counter array before each case and reads it after. A case
that lights a counter no earlier case lit is kept, and later cases are drawn by
mutating what was kept. That is a real feedback loop and it is what
`ring/entries-corpus.txt` was found by.

Four costs, and the fourth is the one that matters:

- The counters cover **the whole binary**, this harness included, so the first
  few cases light regions that have nothing to do with the validation path.
  Saturation makes that harmless rather than absent, and it is why the corpus is
  minimised.
- A counter is a *region*, not an edge: two ways through one region are one bit.
- Reading and resetting the array costs about an order of magnitude per case,
  which is why the recording run is a command somebody runs and not the gate.
- **The symbols exist only in a build carrying `-Cinstrument-coverage`.** So the
  feature is a cargo feature and not a `cfg`: referring to them without the flag
  is a link error rather than a silently absent signal. Every other build — the
  per-commit gate included — has no feedback and says so on its own report line,
  because a run that reported a corpus and had no way to grow one is the exact
  false green this whole file is arranged against.

### `COUNTER_GAP`, and why it is in this section rather than in a footnote

LLVM gives a region a physical counter only when it needs one. A region whose
execution count can be *derived* — an else-arm whose count is its parent's minus
its sibling's — carries an expression instead, and there is nothing in the
counter array for the harness to read. An input that is the first to reach such a
region adds no bit, is not kept, and never reaches the corpus.

This is not hypothetical and it was not predicted. `f_abi::buf::Name::read`'s
`AUTHORITY/NO_SUCH_CAP` arm and `Request::read`'s are both derived regions. The
generator reaches each of them several thousand times per quarter-million cases —
`llvm-cov show` counts 4 190 and 2 820 — and the corpus the signal built covered
**neither**. The measurement is what said so, which is the argument for the
measurement being a separate tool from the feedback rather than the same tool
trusted twice.

The answer is `ENTRIES_SEEDS`: hand-written cases, one per region the signal
cannot see, written to the corpus ahead of the cover, never dropped by
minimisation, each carrying the region it exists for. That is what a seed corpus
is for, and this is the first honest account this repository has of why it needs
one.

### Two more of the same, and the shape of the mistake they make easy

Review found a third. `f_ring::write_serial` stops on a short write, and that
`break` is a derived region: `SINK` is ninety-six bytes and every drawn write
longer than that takes it — `arena bytes copied` runs to five figures in four
thousand cases — while the corpus reached it never. The first version of this
RFC did not record that as a gap. It accounted for the line as *defensive code
nothing can reach*, in the same paragraph that names two regions nothing could
see. A file that has declared a blind spot twice and then explains its own miss
as unreachable code is the failure this whole arrangement is against, and it
failed silently because the number still cleared the bar: 96.74% against 95%.

Seeding it produced the fourth, and the fourth is the argument. Covering the
`break` **uncovered the line under it** — the loop's go-round, which is the same
test's other arm, derived from the same parent — and the corpus entry that had
been reaching it was dropped by the next minimisation as adding nothing, because
what it added was a region the signal cannot see. So the gap is not only that a
region can be missed. It is that a region can be *lost*, by a mechanism that
cannot report having lost it. Two seeds, one per arm, and the figure moved to
96.95%.

Two rules follow, and they are cheap:

- An uncovered line is accounted for **by name and by mechanism**, in the table
  in *What would reverse this*. A count with no list is what let a reachable line
  sit inside the word *unreachable* for a whole review cycle.
- `--record` replays the seeds **first**, in the order the file carries them.
  Before this they were excluded from minimisation and prepended afterwards, so
  three entries survived by lighting what a seed above them already lit, and the
  corpus header's *no entry in it is redundant* was false about its own file.
- A seed earns its place by a **test**, not by an argument. Replay a near-miss
  case and then the reaching case into one process with the signal on: if the
  reaching case is *not kept*, what it reached is invisible and needs a seed. The
  short write is not kept. The two `Table::slot_of` cases are, which is how the
  third seed this file used to carry was found to be insurance against nothing —
  four entries the signal itself kept already reach that region, and removing the
  seed left the figure at 476 of 491. It is gone.

### The denominator, and the one heuristic inside it

`llvm-cov report --show-functions` prints a row per *instantiation*, and rustc
emits an extra row for every generic it did not instantiate in this binary — a
zero-coverage record whose v0 symbol writes the missing type argument as a bare
`p` or `Kp`. Counting those alongside the real instantiation would report every
generic on the path as half covered, so they are dropped. It is not a small
adjustment: it removes 289 of the 780 raw lines the report attributes to the
thirty-seven members, and with it off the figure reads 60.90%.

A substring of a whole mangled symbol is not the same thing as a type argument in
the argument position, so the recogniser can be wrong — and the direction it can
be wrong in matters. Dropping an *uncovered* row raises the figure, which is
exactly the failure `entries_measure` exists to refuse. So the pattern is checked
against what it claims to be true of rather than trusted: every row it drops must
have executed nothing, which a placeholder record does by construction, and a run
where one has an executed line fails naming the symbol. The per-member table
prints how many rows were dropped for each member, so a change in the
denominator is visible rather than inferred.

### `LTO_GAP`

`[profile.release]` carries `lto = true`. Under it, `llvm-cov` reports that
functions have mismatched data and hands back near-zero coverage for functions
that demonstrably ran — `Table::execute` at 42% on a run that executed it fifteen
thousand times, `SetId::from_completion` at 0% on a run that called it once per
case. So the instrumented build sets `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false`, and the
published figure is a figure **about the source** rather than about the machine
code the release actually ships. Stated here rather than discovered next to a
number.

### `FRAME_GAP`

`kernel/src/ring.rs` is the frame's own service and it is not in the path. It
cannot be: the kernel has no host harness at all — `kernel/Cargo.toml` says why —
so no instrument in this repository produces a coverage figure for it, and a
denominator that quietly excluded it while the prose said *the validation path*
would be the same false green one layer up.

What stands in its place is not a percentage and is not offered as one:
`cargo xtask run`'s boot drives the same `f_ring::execute` on the target and
requires both of its refusal paths — an unknown opcode and a forged index-ring
slot — to be answered, in a build with no unwinding and no allocator; and
`cargo xtask runtime`'s fourth boot drives it against a scribbled header. Two
boots against four hundred and ninety-one measured lines is the trade, and the
day the kernel acquires a host harness this gap closes by the path growing rather
than by anything here changing.

### One thing this looked for and did not find

The generation counter's saturation. `retire` uses `saturating_add` so that a
slot's sixty-five thousandth registration runs out of slots rather than reissuing
a name, and the first version of the ledger defect replaced it with
`wrapping_add` — and could not be caught. `Table::register`'s free predicate
already refuses a slot at `RETIRED_GENERATION`, so `retire` is *never asked* to
add to it and the two versions are indistinguishable. The two guards are defence
in depth and exactly one of them is load-bearing; `mutate-reusable-slot` is
therefore in the predicate. Worth recording because the finding is about the
shipped code and not about the harness: a reader of `retire` would reasonably
believe its saturation is what prevents the bug, and it is not.

## Consequences

**What it makes easy.** A regression in the validation path's *behaviour* now
fails as a named oracle with a one-line reproduction, rather than as a
plausible-looking completion nobody reads. A regression in its *coverage* fails
as a claim, with a per-member table saying which function fell. A new branch in
any of the thirty-seven functions is a line nothing reaches and shows up as the
number falling — which makes the claim a test of code that has not been written
yet.

**What it makes hard.** Adding a function to the path means adding it in two
places, and the check that requires both is deliberate friction. Moving one of
the five files, or renaming a function in it, breaks the symbol fragments in
`ENTRIES_PATH` — and that fails loudly with the report's own output quoted,
rather than silently shrinking the denominator.

**What it forecloses.** Using the shipped release profile for the measurement, as
long as `lto = true` and llvm-cov disagree. And a *whole-file* coverage figure for
these crates: `abi/src/buf.rs` and `ring/src/registry.rs` contain plenty that is
not entry validation, so a per-file number would be a different and weaker claim
wearing the same words.

**What it costs to run.** The gate is 262 144 drawn cases at about 2.5 s, inside
`cargo xtask verify` — which is 8 min 17 s in all with it. The coverage
measurement rebuilds three crates instrumented and with LTO off: about 40 s on a
cold target directory, 9.6 s warm, so it is a CI step of its own. The mutation
harness is 42 s. The recording run draws a million cases with the signal on and
took 2 min 09 s and 2 min 16 s over two runs; it is nobody's gate.

## What would reverse this

- **A member of the path that cannot be reached and cannot be argued away.**
  Fifteen lines of the four hundred and ninety-one are missed, and every one of
  them is a second bound behind a check that already refused. The list, because
  a count is not an account and the first version of this paragraph carried one
  without the other:

  | lines | where | why nothing reaches it |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | 5 | `execute`, the `_` opcode arm | `op::known` admitted the opcode two lines above and this build implements both arms it admits |
  | 2 | `write_serial` | a `u64` offset that does not fit a `usize`, which no 64-bit host produces; and the arena refusing a range `write_serial` had already bounded |
  | 1 | `Table::slot_of`, generation zero | `Name::read` and `Request::read` both refuse a generation-zero id before `slot_of` is asked for one |
  | 1 | `Table::issued`, its `Err` arm | its only caller hands it an id `Table::register` minted one line earlier |
  | 3 | `negotiated_for`, `Registered::bind`, `BufferSet::bind` | one `Err` arm each, summed over the instantiation whose transport requires no feature, where the arm cannot be taken at all |
  | 3 | `BufferSet::carve`, the zero-buffer refusal | summed over the instantiations whose `B` is a non-zero constant |

  They are counted in the denominator and the figure clears 95% with them in it.
  If that stops being true — if defensive unreachable code grows to where the
  number cannot clear the bar honestly — the answer is to *state which lines are
  unreachable and why*, in this file, and to lower the threshold to what remains.
  It is not to delete the members.

  **What this paragraph got wrong the first time, and what it cost.** It said
  fifteen while sixteen were missed, and it named `write_serial`'s short-write
  `break` among the unreachable ones. That line is reachable: `SINK` is 96 bytes
  and any write longer than that takes it, which the generator does thousands of
  times per gate run. It was uncovered because the *corpus* did not reach it, and
  the reason it did not is `COUNTER_GAP` — a third instance of the same gap, in a
  file that had already declared the gap twice and then accounted for its own
  miss as defensive code. That is the failure mode this repository is arranged
  against, arriving in prose beside a number rather than in the number: the
  measurement stayed green because 96.74% clears 95%, and the sentence explaining
  the shortfall was the only thing that was wrong. It is two seeds now — the arm
  and its sibling, which seeding the first one uncovered — the figure is 96.95%,
  and the reversal condition it teaches is written above the table: an uncovered
  line is accounted for *by name*, or it is a finding.
- **A byte-level family that finds something the structure-aware families do
  not.** The eighth is a hedge against the families being a guess. If the hedge
  ever pays, the proportion is wrong and the argument in *Context* is wrong with
  it — and the honest response is to raise the byte share and say what changed.
- **A second thread.** Every case here is single-threaded, so no oracle in this
  file can see a race. `ring/tests/hostile.rs` declares the same limit as
  `PEER_GAP`. A property about concurrent validation needs a different instrument
  — Miri's preemption — and a different property.
- **`COUNTER_GAP` closing.** If a future toolchain gives every region a physical
  counter, or exposes the expression map at runtime, the seeds stop being needed
  and `ENTRIES_SEEDS` should shrink to nothing rather than being kept out of
  habit. The measurement is what would say so: a `--record` run whose corpus
  covers 96.95% without them.
- **The feedback signal becoming path-aware.** The counter array covers the whole
  binary, this harness included, so an entry kept for lighting something new may
  have lit something new *in the harness*, and minimisation therefore keeps
  entries the published number does not need. Measured, not feared: a
  leave-one-out over the forty-one committed entries — each replayed as
  corpus-minus-one through the same pipeline — leaves the figure at 476 of 491
  for twelve of them. The sharpest instance is on the face of the file: one entry
  is the *same case* as a seed above it, written without a field the seed writes
  explicitly, and it survives because the two argvs take different branches
  through the harness's own argument parser. That is why the corpus header and
  `--corpus`'s report both say *a region of this binary* and not *of the
  validation path*: the stronger sentence is not what the mechanism checks.
  Intersecting the counter set with the regions belonging to the thirty-seven
  members would make it true, at the cost of a region-to-function map the runtime
  does not hand out — `llvm-cov export` does, per run rather than per case. It is
  worth doing the day the corpus is large enough that reading it is work; today
  the per-member table is what tells a needed entry from a kept one, and a
  weaker sentence that is true beats a stronger one nobody checks.
- **A coverage figure that stops meaning anything because the corpus is tuned to
  it.** This is the standing risk with any coverage gate, and the mitigation here
  is that the number is not the only thing checked: three oracles with a defect
  each, thirty-seven reach minimums, and a corpus that must replay clean. A
  corpus grown to touch lines rather than to catch anything would still have to
  pass all of those. If somebody finds a way to make it pass them anyway, that is
  the reversal.
